description: Trigger discrimination for runtime per-call context curation (this skill) vs session-start context loading (agent-startup-context-gate), spend caps (ai-cost-guardrail-designer), retrieval authorization (rag-security-architect), redaction mechanics (sensitive-disclosure-guard), the in-batch call-gating and agent instruction custody seam (agent-harness-architect), the output schema a prompt contract points to (structured-output-validator), running an evaluation rerun (ai-evaluation-harness, manual-only), injection defense (prompt-injection-defender, manual-only), and the DESIGN-vs-REVIEW seam against memory-context-poisoning-reviewer.

cases.prompt: Decide what goes into our model's context each call: which segments from which sources, assembled server-side under hard token caps with a designed truncation order, sensitive values excluded from controlled application stores, provider retention checked, exclusions documented, and what it saw reconstructible afterward.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (primary) — segments, caps, schemas, the persisted/transient split, reconstructibility, and designed exclusions are the curation contract. No session-start verification, no budget authoring, no retrieval authz is requested.
cases.reason: The subject is per-call context content: what enters and leaves the window. The cost of the capped space and the authorization of the retriever are consumed from their owning skills, not designed here.

cases.prompt: Before the agent starts work in this repository, verify it is the intended repo from the git remote and landmark files, read the project instructions and status docs, and separate verified facts from assumptions.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (pinned) — session-START context: proving the agent is in the right place with current governing docs before any work. A different moment from per-call window assembly, with a different failure mode (building in the wrong place vs feeding the model wrong content).
cases.reason: Startup verification and context loading are agent-startup-context-gate. model-context-designer owns the RUNTIME per-call assembly of the model's window.

cases.prompt: Set the token budgets for our AI feature: per-request input/output caps, per-tenant monthly budgets, cost-aware rate limits, and a kill switch before the bill explodes.
cases.note: SEAM CASE — the cap is a COST decision; the curation is a CONTENT decision. This prompt is entirely about pricing and bounding spend.
cases.reason: Budgets, caps-as-policy, and rate limits are ai-cost-guardrail-designer. model-context-designer decides what the capped space carries, consuming those caps as an input.

cases.prompt: Make sure our vector search only ever returns documents the calling user and tenant are allowed to see, enforced in the query itself, with per-tenant index scoping.
cases.reason: Authorization at retrieval time and vector-store tenant scoping are rag-security-architect. model-context-designer curates what the already-authorized retrieval feeds into the window.

cases.prompt: Add pre-model redaction of secrets and PII, check the output paths for echoed sensitive data, and redact the logs at emission.
cases.reason: Redaction mechanics and output-path echo/bleed checks are sensitive-disclosure-guard. model-context-designer decides the context diet those controls apply to — minimization decisions, not redaction implementation.

cases.prompt: Every model call should be gated before it runs: identity from credentials, a deny-by-default authorize/entitlement/budget ladder, a closed tool registry, and a fail-closed audit write.
cases.note: IN-BATCH SEAM (pinned both ways) — the harness gates the CALL; this skill curates the CONTENT that rides in it. Nothing here asks what fills the window.
cases.reason: Mediation, the pre-flight ladder, registry, and audit are agent-harness-architect. model-context-designer owns what enters and leaves the window of a call the harness has already gated.

cases.prompt: Write a prompt contract for our summarizer: the instruction's version and owner, its declared inputs, a pointer to its output schema, when it must decline, and which prompt edits need an evaluation rerun.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (D70 extension) — the prompt contract record ties the parts together and points to their owners. The output schema is only referenced, no evaluation is run, no agent harness is being wired, and no injection defense is asked for.
cases.reason: Writing the versioned, owned prompt contract with declared inputs, decline conditions and a change policy is model-context-designer. structured-output-validator owns the schema it points to; ai-evaluation-harness runs the reruns it calls for.

cases.prompt: We are editing our classifier prompt to add a new category. Update the prompt contract: bump the version, say whether this edit needs an evaluation rerun, and add a decline condition for inputs that fit no category.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (D70 extension) — deciding WHETHER a prompt change needs a rerun is the contract's change policy; running it is not requested.
cases.reason: The version bump, change-policy classification and decline conditions are the prompt contract. The rerun it requires is then run under ai-evaluation-harness (manual-only).

cases.prompt: Define the JSON output schema for our summarizer with field types, enums and ranges, and validate every response before our code uses it, rejecting failures instead of repairing them silently.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (D70 extension) — the output contract and validate-before-use ladder. The prompt contract only points to it.
cases.reason: The output schema and its validation are structured-output-validator. model-context-designer's prompt contract references that contract by pointer and never restates it.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke ai-evaluation-harness. Our summarizer prompt changed from version 3 to 4; run the regression suite with the quality and refusal graders and block the release if it regresses.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (D70 extension) — RUNNING the evaluation gate on a prompt change. The prompt contract only says when a rerun is needed.
cases.reason: Datasets, graders, thresholds and the regression gate are ai-evaluation-harness (manual-only, because runs spend tokens). model-context-designer's change policy decides that a rerun is needed, not how it runs.

cases.prompt: Our agent's system instructions are pasted into client code. Move them to server-side versioned artifacts that no user can override, and record which instruction version served each call.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (D70 extension) — custody of an agent's instructions and the per-call served version belong to the harness. An agent's prompt contract points to that version.
cases.reason: Instructions as server-side versioned artifacts with the serving version recorded per call are agent-harness-architect. model-context-designer writes the contract that references the version, not the custody mechanism.

cases.prompt: Review our agent's memory and stored context for poisoning: can a user's message get persisted as a trusted fact, survive into later sessions, or bleed into another tenant's context?
cases.note: DESIGN-vs-REVIEW SEAM (mandatory) — this is the attack review of stored context/memory. model-context-designer PRODUCES the curated-context artifact that reviewer examines; it never runs the poisoning audit.
cases.reason: Poisoning, cross-session trust, and cross-tenant bleed of stored context are memory-context-poisoning-reviewer's lane. This skill designs the curated context in the first place.
